beats.say: Y equals four X plus two, over X plus one, for X greater than negative one. The line Y equals C misses this curve.
asks: What are we asked to explain?

beats.say: First, what the question says. This is the curve, drawn only where X is greater than negative one.
asks: Why only x greater than negative one?

beats.say: Y equals C is a horizontal line, at height C. It never touches the curve, anywhere.
asks: Why is y = c a horizontal line?

beats.say: We must explain why C is at least four, by writing the fraction as A plus B over X plus one.
asks: Why write it in this form?

beats.say: Then the sign of B over X plus one tells us where the curve sits.
To get that form, write the top using X plus one, so that part of it divides exactly by the bottom.
asks: Why write the top using x + 1?
Can I use long division instead?

beats.say: Four lots of X plus one make four X plus four. That is two too many, so take away two.
Split it into two fractions. In the first, X plus one is a factor of the top and the bottom, so it equals four.
asks: Why can we split the fraction?

beats.say: So Y equals four minus two over X plus one. A is four, and B is negative two.
Now the sign. Since X is greater than negative one, X plus one is greater than zero.
Two over a positive number is positive, so two over X plus one is greater than zero.
asks: Why is 2 over a positive number positive?

beats.say: Times by negative one, and the sign flips: negative two over X plus one is less than zero.
So Y equals four minus two over X plus one: four take away a positive number, so less than four.
Think of the graph: the curve is always below the line Y equals four.
As X grows, the curve gets closer and closer to four, but never touches it.
Now slide the line Y equals C down below four, say C equals one. Now it cuts the curve.
Near X equals negative one the curve goes down forever, so every line below four cuts it.
asks: Why does every line below 4 cut the curve?

beats.say: At C equals four, it still misses: the curve never touches four. So C equals four is allowed.
Above four, it misses too. So the line must be at four or above: C is greater than or equal to four.
